text:
Jonathan Lekkerimäki had three points in 13 NHL games last season. He has 18 in 23 this year, and the people around him have noticed. Daily Faceoff wrote about him "realizing his potential," and Brock Boeser told Pass it to Bulis that "For how little he is, he has a super-hard shot."

The power play is where it's happening: 11 of his 18 points have come with the man advantage, and his ice time is up more than two minutes a night over his last ten games, including a stint beside Elias Pettersson and Boeser. Forwards picked 10th to 20th since 2005 scored a median 0.35 points a game in their first full season. He's at 0.78.

Some of it is running hot. He has seven goals on 4.6 expected (17.9% shooting), and at 5v5 the Canucks get only 39% of the expected goals (chance quality) with him on the ice. Last season's tiny sample from Evolving-Hockey said offense dried up with him out there. But his goals have added more wins than all but 52 skaters, and on a Vancouver team that lost seven straight before this week, that's worth a lot.
headline: Lekkerimäki and that shot
